title.narrative: Provide risk management coordination and support across UN agencies in Somalia.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe Risk Management Unit (RMU) is a specialised hub that provides independent risk management tools and services to donors, programming partners (including the Somali Humanitarian Fund), and UN entities. It facilitates information sharing, collective risk management, and accountability across Somalia's complex operating environment. By addressing sensitive and complex issues related to situational awareness and analysis, corruption and aid diversion, the RMU enhances operational integrity, safeguards impact, delivers exceptional value for money by strengthening the effectiveness of international support.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtThe RMU plays a central role in aligning project controls across UN agencies, fostering inter-agency cooperation in procurement oversight, due diligence, and risk harmonisation. Through standardised methodologies and shared frameworks, the RMU strengthens coherence in managing operational and fiduciary risks. As a key enabler of programme assurance, it promotes transparency, accountability, and collective resilience, ensuring unified and effective risk-informed decision-making across the UN system.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIn this project, the RMU will strengthen system-wide risk management, accountability, and decision-making across the humanitarian response in Somalia by providing due diligence tools and information, risk analysis, and capacity development services that directly support SHF and benefit all implementing partners working with UN agencies. The RMU will conduct regular Partner Verification Reports and ad-hoc due diligence assessments, providing the UNCT, SHF, and humanitarian partners with reliable assurance on partner integrity. This will inform funding, procurement, and programmatic decisions while reducing fraud, aid diversion, and operational risk. ltbrgtltbrgtIt will maintain and enhance core risk intelligence tools—including CIMS, CIRT, the Aid Diversion Tracker, RiskIQ (an AI-powered risk advisor), and a unified RMU Portal—ensuring timely risk analysis, alerts, and reports that improve procurement oversight, coordination, compliance, and proactive risk mitigation. These tools will offer SHF implementing partners and UN agency partners centralized access to risk information, predictive insights, and capacity injection data, supporting more efficient use of donor resources and reducing duplication. ltbrgtltbrgtThe RMU will also deliver targeted NGO risk and accountability trainings, workshops, and an annual risk summit to strengthen national and international partner capacities and promote collaboration and shared learning. Finally, the RMU will lead inter-agency risk governance through working groups, UNCT/HCT briefings, and participation in key coordination forums, fostering coherent, risk-informed humanitarian operations. Through these activities, the RMU will enhance transparency, safeguard humanitarian assistance, and enable SHF and all UN-supported implementing partners to deliver aid more effectively and responsibly in complex, high-risk environments.ltbrgtlt/pgt
